title: Structured intake and prioritization for org security & admin access requests (RBAC, SSO, SCIM)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers repeatedly submit a mix of admin/access requests (RBAC role changes, SSO/SAML setup, SCIM provisioning, org-level policy exceptions) through disparate channels (support email, sales threads, CSM notes). This causes slow response, inconsistent prioritization, and missed compliance audits.

Goal: Define a single, enforceable intake form + triage rubric and routing rules for non-bug admin/access requests so that: (1) requests are correctly classified within 24h; (2) high-impact security requests are escalated to Security/Platform within 4 business hours; (3) expected response and SLA windows are communicated to the customer at intake.

Success metrics: 
- 95% of new admin/access requests have an intake record and classification within 24 hours.
- Mean time to first meaningful response reduced from current ~48h to <12h.
- >80% of requests routed correctly to Eng/Security/PM/CS without reassignments.

Stakeholders: 
- Product (PM): Aisha Patel (owner)
- Eng (Platform & IAM): Diego Morales (assignee), Eng rotation for triage
- Security: Priya Iyer (review & escalation)
- Customer Success: Rahul Mehta (CSM intake touchpoint)
- Legal/Compliance: Emily Novak (audit & policy)

Proposed intake fields (single canonical form used by support/CS/sales):
- Customer org name (string)
- Point of contact + role (string)
- Request type (enum): [RBAC-role-change, RBAC-policy-exception, SSO/SAML-setup, SCIM-provisioning, Org-policy-request, Other]
- Detailed description / business justification (multiline)
- Affected users or groups (list)
- Desired timeline / deadline (date + business-urgency flag)
- Data sensitivity (enum): [none, low, medium, high, regulated]
- Regulatory impact (enum): [none, GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, PCI, other]
- Attached artifacts (link list): audit logs, screenshots, SAML metadata, SCIM schema examples
- Customer tier / contract (enum): [Self-serve, Startup, Growth, Enterprise]
- Suggested outcome (free text)

Triage and prioritization rubric (scoring):
- Urgency score (0-4): immediate outage or security incident ->4; deadline within 48h ->3; requested within 2 weeks ->2; no SLA ->0-1
- Impact score (0-4): regulated data or >100 users affected ->4; >10 users or org-wide setting ->3; single user->1
- Compliance score (0-3): regulatory scope ->3; audit required ->2; none->0
- Operational complexity penalty (-0-2): breaking changes or migrations ->+2

Priority calculation: Weighted sum = 0.45*Urgency + 0.35*Impact + 0.2*Compliance + Complexity. Map to triage buckets: P0 (immediate security incident), P1 (high), P2 (medium), P3 (low/feature request).

Routing rules (automation + manual guardrails):
- If Urgency>=4 or Impact>=4 or Data sensitivity==regulated -> assign to Security + Platform + PM, Escalate to on-call Security within 4h.
- If Request type is SSO/SAML-setup and Customer tier==Enterprise -> assign to Eng IAM + CS + PM; create pre-config checklist (see artifacts).
- If Request type is RBAC-policy-exception -> route to PM + Platform; require org admin approval and legal signoff if Compliance score>0.
- SCIM provisioning requests for Enterprise tier create a staged plan (scoped rollout) with QA and migration windows.

Expected SLAs (to be communicated at intake):
- Acknowledgement: within 4 business hours for high, 24h for others.
- Initial assessment and owner assignment: 24h.
- Proposed plan (if not immediate): within 5 business days.

Canned responses & customer comms templates (examples included in repository):
- Acknowledgement (auto): "Thanks — we received your request. A PM will review and reply with next steps within 24 hours."
- Security escalation: "We take this seriously. Your request has been escalated to our Security team and an engineer will contact you within 4 hours."

Audit/data retention: All intake records must persist and be exportable for compliance audits (CSV/JSON). The form must capture who approved any org-policy exception and when.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Intake form implemented in Zendesk/Intercom/HubSpot stub or internal intake tool and integrated with Linear ticket creation.
2) Triage rubric implemented as a lightweight rule engine (initially in a Google Sheet or internal Airtable) producing suggested bucket, with manual override and recorded rationale.
3) Routing automation prototypes (Zapier/Workato or internal webhook) that create correct assignees and add Security when thresholds met.
4) CS and Sales training doc + templates published.
5) One pilot run with 3 Enterprise customers and post-pilot retrospective with metrics.

Next steps: 
- Week 1: finalize intake fields with CS and Security (owner: Aisha).
- Week 2: prototype rule spreadsheet and mapping table (owner: Diego).
- Week 3: implement webhook for ticket creation + initial canned responses (owner: Eng rotation).
- Week 4: pilot with two Enterprise customers and collect metrics (owner: Rahul).

Notes / constraints: Some customers require on-prem connector for SCIM; that will be a separate engineering project with a longer timeline. Where legal signoff is needed, workflow must include Legal as approver before changes are applied.
